8. Data management systems

System Key facts
GFS / HDFS Master / NameNode; chunk server / DataNode; chunk / block (64 MB in lecture); 3 replicas on different racks; read → metadata of one replica; append → all replicas, primary picks offset; heartbeats

Parallel DB architectures Shared memory (SMP) · shared disk (NAS/SAN) · shared nothing

2. One-line distinctions

  • Grid harnesses unused cycles across organizations; cluster = interconnected stand-alone computers acting as one resource.
  • Utility computing = concept (metered); cloud = its realization.
  • Elasticity = up and down; scale-up (bigger box, cheaper small) vs scale-out (more boxes, only option large).
  • Client–server: no virtualization; cloud: virtualization is core.
  • On-site private: limited resources, high up-front cost; outsourced private: two perimeters, extensive resources.
  • Para-virtualization modifies the guest; full translates binaries; hardware-assisted uses Intel VT/AMD-V.
  • DOS (metadata, cloud manager) vs PLS (persistent VM storage, cluster manager).
  • Well-formed (syntax) vs valid (+ schema); DTD (entities, non-XML) vs XSD (XML, types, no entities).
  • SAX (events, fast, low memory) vs DOM (tree, slow, modifiable).
  • SOAP messaging · WSDL description · UDDI registry.
  • KPI → SLO → SLA; off-the-shelf SLA unsuitable for mission-critical.
  • GFS read: one replica’s metadata; append: all replicas, primary chooses offset.
  • BigTable bulk, GFS-based; Dynamo key–value, small concurrent updates, quorum.
  • Mapper failure → redo its whole task; reducer failure → only unfinished tasks.
  • Swift object vs Cinder block; Glance images; Keystone identity; Ceilometer metering.
  • Web role (front end) vs worker role (background), linked by queues.
  • App Engine PaaS vs Compute Engine IaaS.
  • RPO (data loss) vs RTO (recovery time).
  • Interception = confidentiality; modification = integrity; fabrication = authenticity; interruption = availability.
  • Traffic analysis passive; replay active.
  • MAUI (annotated methods) vs COMET (binaries, DSM threads).
  • Cloudlet = single-hop middle tier; fog = Cisco’s term; dew = works offline (independence + collaboration).
  • Bursting/broker loose; aggregated partial; multi-tier tight.
  • Cold migration: downtime = migration time; pre-copy: memory first; post-copy: CPU first.
  • Container (OS-level, shared kernel) vs VM (hardware-level, guest OS); image vs container.
  • FaaS (your functions) vs BaaS (provider’s back-end services).
  • eMBB (AR/VR) · URLLC (autonomous/telesurgery) · mMTC (massive IoT).
  • One-to-many virtual sensor (middleware sets sampling) vs derived (combine different sensor types).

Week 1 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 1 notes

  • NIST: 5 characteristics (on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service) · 3 service models · 4 deployment models.
  • Utility computing = metered, charge per use (concept) → cloud realizes it. Five utility risks: backup, security, competence, SLA definition, charge-back.
  • Grid = unused cycles / single system image (power-grid analogy); cluster = stand-alone computers as one resource (HA, load-balancing, parallel).
  • Client–server: no virtualization; cloud: virtualization is core, theoretically infinite scaling.
  • Provider responsibility: IaaS → virtualization; PaaS → runtime; SaaS → application. OSI: IaaS → data link; PaaS → presentation; SaaS → all.
  • Scale-out is the only solution at large scale (64 × 1-way ≪ one 64-way server).
  • Lecture classifications: Azure = PaaS, App Engine = PaaS, EC2 = IaaS, Salesforce/Google Docs = SaaS.
  • SaaS not for real-time; PaaS risk = vendor lock-in; IaaS not when highest dedicated performance is needed.

Likely question types (from the lectures): pick the non-NIST characteristic · classify a product into IaaS/PaaS/SaaS · where is X not suitable · scale-up vs scale-out.

Week 2 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 2 notes

  • Public: low up-front cost, multi-tenancy risk, restrictive default SLA. On-site private: limited resources, significant–high cost. Outsourced private: two perimeters, extensive resources. On-site community: highly variable cost.
  • Hybrid constituents remain unique entities; hybrid can be extremely complex; members join/leave.
  • IaaS hierarchy: Cloud manager (+DOS) → Cluster manager (+PLS) → Computer manager (per host).
  • Popek–Goldberg: equivalence, resource control, efficiency; VMM possible if sensitive ⊆ privileged.
  • Full (binary translation, QEMU/Bochs, portable) · Para (modified guest, Xen, faster) · HW-assisted (Intel VT/AMD-V, unmodified guest, ring 0).
  • XML: valid ⇒ well-formed; XSD (2001, written in XML, no entities); xmlns; SAX events/fast vs DOM tree/memory.
  • SOAP (stateless, one-way, HTTP) · WSDL (describe) · UDDI (registry); SOA = publish–find–bind (IBM).

Likely question types: deployment-model consideration matching · which component does X in IaaS hierarchy · virtualization type from a description · well-formed vs valid · SOAP/WSDL/UDDI matching.

Week 3 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 3 notes

  • KPI → SLO → SLA; off-the-shelf SLA unsuitable for mission-critical; cloud SLA needs automation; neutral third-party monitoring.
  • Cv​=σ/∣μ∣; n independent loads → Cv​/n​.
  • Cloud cheaper ⇔ U=C/B<P/A; penalty ∝∫∣D−R∣; exponential demand ⇒ exponential penalty.
  • P(fail)=1−(1−p)N → fault tolerance essential.
  • GFS read: one replica’s metadata; append: all replicas, primary chooses offset; master = NameNode, chunk server = DataNode; 3 replicas.
  • Dynamo: key–value, MD5 ring, R+W>N; BigTable: row/column/timestamp, tablets, SSTables.
  • Word count: split words 1/p (not scalable) vs split docs 1/(1+2p/nf); MR 1/(1+2cσ/w).
  • OpenStack: Nova compute, Neutron network, Swift object, Cinder block, Keystone identity, Glance image, Ceilometer metering, Horizon dashboard.

Lecture-solved problems & variants

  • Quorum (L13). N=3: is (R,W)=(2,2) consistent? Yes: 2+2=4>3. Variant: N=5, (R,W)=(2,3)? No: 5>5; need e.g. (3,3).
  • Aggregation (Cv​). 100 independent workloads with Cv​=0.5 each. Aggregate Cv​? 0.5/100​=0.05. Variant: 49 workloads, Cv​=0.7? 0.7/7=0.1.
  • Utility pricing. P=100, A=25, C=0.30, B=0.10. Cloud or own? U=3<P/A=4 → cloud. Variant: P=60, A=40, U=2? P/A=1.5<2 → own.
  • Failure probability. p=0.001, N=1000? 1−0.9991000≈0.63.

Week 4 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 4 notes

  • Security group = in + out firewall rules per VM; VM gets an internal IP, associate an external (floating) IP for outside access; terminate deletes & releases resources.
  • Meghamala: 3 flavours (Regular/Large/Extra Large), 3 OS (Ubuntu/CentOS/Fedora); Meghadoop (Hadoop), Meghadata (Dropbox-like).
  • Azure: Windows Azure + SQL Azure + AppFabric; web role (front end) vs worker role (background) via storage queues; ≥ 1 role of either type.
  • Azure deploy: deployment user → resource group (logical container) → App Service plan (location/size/features) → web app (*.azurewebsites.net) → git push.
  • GCP: App Engine = PaaS, Compute Engine = IaaS; Cloud Storage (object), Cloud SQL (MySQL), Datastore (NoSQL).
  • Static site = Cloud Storage bucket + index.html + 404.html + public sharing; App Engine app = app.yaml (+ threadsafe) + main.py → gcloud app deploy.

Likely question types: which OpenStack service backs a dashboard item · resource group vs App Service plan · web vs worker role · GCP service ↔︎ model.

Week 5 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 5 notes

  • Availability =(1−d/T)×100 with T = scheduled hours; credit from the band; payable = bill − credit.
  • CSCC 7 steps; NIST 5 actors (consumer, provider, carrier, broker, auditor); fault domain vs update domain vs availability set.
  • HDFS blocks = ⌈size/block⌉ × replication.
  • MapReduce average: mappers emit (avg, count).
  • Consolidate VMs; idle servers waste power; Wake-on-LAN; minimal VM images (38 → 8 s; 4 GB → 600 MB).
  • RM aspects: provisioning, allocation, adaptation, mapping, modelling, estimation, discovery, brokering, scheduling.

Lecture-solved problems & variants

  • SLA P1 (L21). Guarantee 99 %, 12 h/day × 30 days, outage 10.75 h. Violated? T=360 h; lecture: 1−10.75/349.25=96.92% (standard 97.01 %) < 99 % → violated. Variant: guarantee 99.5 %, 10 h/day × 30 days, outage 2 h? 1−2/300=99.33% < 99.5 % → violated.
  • SLA P2 (L21). $50/day, 30 days, 12 h/day, credit 10 % if 99–99.95 %, 25 % if < 99 %; outages total 9 h 25 min. Payable? A=97.385% → 25 % of $1500 = $375 → $1125. Variant: $40/day, measured 99.2 %? Bill $1200, credit 10 % = $120 → $1080.
  • Allowed downtime. 99.9 % over a 30-day, 24 h month? 0.001×720=0.72 h = 43.2 min.
  • Economics P1 (L22). D=50sint / 20sint, R=D+δD′, δ=π/12. Penalty? Lecture: 30π/12≈ 7.86 (strict ∫∣D−R∣=70π/12≈18.33).
  • Economics P2 (L22). D=50(1+e−t), P=100, B=120, C=200, T=100? BT​=1.2 M, CT​≈1.01 M, ratio 0.84 → cloud cheaper.
  • Economics P3 (L22). In-house ₹6 lakh/3 yr, 12 cores, 40 %, +₹22 power, +₹6 mgmt; cloud ₹42/h, 8 cores, 80 %, +₹1. Core-hour & ratio? ₹1.90 vs ₹5.25 per core-h; totals 85.075 vs 53.5 → 1.59; in-house wins only at ≈ 90 % efficiency. Variant: in-house efficiency 60 %? 22.83/0.6+28=66.05 vs 53.5 → cloud still cheaper.
  • HDFS (L23). 64 MB blocks, ×3; files 64 KB, 65 MB, 127 MB? 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 blocks → 15 stored. Variant: 128 MB blocks, ×3; files 100 MB, 130 MB, 300 MB? 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 → 18.
  • MapReduce average (L23). {10, 20}, {30, 40}, {50}? (15·2 + 35·2 + 50·1)/5 = 30, not 33.3.
  • Consolidation (L24). Idle 105 W, full (8 VMs) 170 W, 2 VMs 138 W; 4 nodes, 8 VMs? Spread 552 W; packed 485 W; packed + 3 off 170 W.

From your L21 practice set (file w2): same template, new values

  • Allowed downtime at 99 % of 360 h (Q6)? 0.01×360=3.6 h, so the 10.75 h outage violates the SLA.
  • Problem 2 with only 3 h of downtime (Q15)? 357/360=99.17% → between 99 % and 99.95 % → 10 % credit.
  • Exactly 99.00 % (Q33)? The band is “≥ 99 % and < 99.95 %” → 10 %: the boundary belongs to the upper band.
  • 99.2 % on the $1500 bill (Q46)? 10 % credit = $150 → $1350.
  • 99.5 % over 720 h, in minutes (Q32)? 0.005×720=3.6 h = 216 min.
  • 99.8 % over a 30-day month (Q42)? 0.002×720=1.44 h (≈ 86 min). Variants: 99.95 % over 720 h? 21.6 min. · Exactly 99.95 % in Problem 2? Not below 99.95 % → no credit. · 98.9 % on $60/day × 30 days? Bill $1800, 25 % credit = $450 → $1350.

Week 6 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 6 notes

  • Interruption→availability · interception→confidentiality · modification→integrity · fabrication→authenticity.
  • Disclosure (snooping) · deception (spoofing, repudiation, denial of receipt) · disruption · usurpation (delay, DoS).
  • Passive (release of contents, traffic analysis, hard to detect) vs active (masquerade, replay, modification, DoS).
  • Secure R⊆Q · precise R=Q · broad otherwise.
  • Cloud-specific: co-tenancy, lack of control, reputation fate-sharing; IDC 2008: security top concern.
  • Gartner 7: privileged user access, compliance & audit, data location, data segregation, recovery, investigative support, long-term viability. RPO = data loss; RTO = recovery time.
  • EC2 study: placement → extraction; co-residency = same Dom0, small RTT, IPs within 7; ~40 % success; probes on ports 80/443.
  • Collaborative SaaS: SelCSP, risk-based access (fuzzy), IDRM (NP-hard → greedy), conflicts (cyclic inheritance, SoD). Broker: fuzzy (QoS + trust → suitability); migrate if SLA satisfaction < threshold.

Likely question types: attack ↔︎ property · threat class · passive vs active · Gartner list “which is NOT” · RPO vs RTO · co-residency indicators.

Week 7 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 7 notes

  • MCC = cloud + mobile + wireless; profiler (time/power/traffic) → solver (placement) → synchronizer (merge).
  • MAUI (annotate remoteable methods; native stays local; RPC) vs COMET (binaries only; DSM thread migration).
  • Cloudlet = trusted, resource-rich, nearby, single-hop, middle tier.
  • Esaved​=MC​(Pc​−Pi​/F)−Ptr​BD​ — offload when compute-heavy, data-light.
  • Fog = Cisco term; enablers: virtualization, containers, SOA, SDN (OpenFlow).
  • Cloud vs fog: latency high/low, hops multi/one, location awareness no/yes, centralized/distributed, few/very many nodes, mobility limited/supported, leased line/wireless.
  • Geospatial cloud: SDI, interoperability at data/service/security levels; Bankura road & water merges.

Lecture-based problem & variant

  • Offloading. C/M=2 s, Pc​=1 W, Pi​=0.2 W, F=20, Ptr​=1.5 W, D/B=1 s? $2(1 - 0.01) - 1.5 = $ 0.48 J saved → offload. Variant: same but D/B=2 s? 1.98−3.0=−1.02 J → don’t offload.

Week 8 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 8 notes

  • Docker (Mar 2013): develop–ship–run anywhere; image = package, container = running instance; Engine / Hub (registry) / Compose.
  • Containers share the host kernel, tens of MB, near-instant start.
  • DC energy: cooling 45 %, IT 40 %, power distribution 15 %; idle server ≈ 66 % of peak; switch: chassis 36 %, line cards 43 %, ports 11 %.
  • PUE = total facility / IT (ideal 1.0).
  • Sensor cloud: sensors = interface, clusters = backbone, Internet = medium; virtual sensors one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many, derived.
  • IoT: unique IDs, no human interaction; things → gateway → cloud; MQTT/CoAP/HTTP (IoT), MQTT/AMQP/HTTP (cloud).

Problem & variant

  • PUE. Total 1.5 MW, IT 600 kW? 2.5 (DCiE 40 %). Variant: total 1.2 MW, IT 1.0 MW? 1.2.

Week 9 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 9 notes

  • Health case: levels cloud (0) – ISP (1) – area gateway (2) – mobile (3) – sensors (4); fog placement: filtering/processing/event handling at area gateway, confirmatory in cloud; fog → low network use, low cloud cost, stable latency. CloudSim (Melbourne); iFogSim (IIT KGP + Melbourne).
  • Fog environment: client, fog, cloud; fog forwards to cloud if short of resources.
  • RM taxonomy: Architecture (data flow, control, tenancy) · Infrastructure (hardware, system software, middleware) · Algorithms (discovery, benchmarking, load balancing, placement).
  • Placement constraints: resource / network / application (locality, deadlines). Control: centralized (solver, graph matching) vs distributed (blockchain, game theory, GA).
  • Federation: bursting & broker = loose, aggregated = partial, multi-tier = tight; cross-site VM migration needs tight coupling.
  • Migration reasons: load balancing, maintenance, power, QoS, fault tolerance. Cold vs live; pre-copy (memory first) vs post-copy (CPU first).

Likely question types: module placement in fog vs cloud · taxonomy pillar matching · federation architecture ↔︎ coupling · pre-copy termination conditions.

Week 10 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 10 notes

  • r=PD/R; Tmig​=RVm​​1−r1−rn+1​+Tres​; Tdown​=rnRVm​​+Tres​; cold: Tdown​=Tmig​=Vm​/R.
  • KVM, Xen, VMware use pre-copy. Parallel multi-VM: each gets R/m; serial: others suspended at first VM’s stop-copy.
  • Containers: OS-level, relaxed isolation, shared kernel; benefits = separation of responsibilities, portability, isolation.
  • Kubernetes (Google, “helmsman”): cluster → worker nodes → Pods; control plane; not monolithic.
  • Docker: client + daemon (REST/HTTP), private registry vs Docker Hub; build, run, commit, tag, save/load.

Problems & variants

  • Cold migration. 2048 MB at 128 MB/s? Tmig​=Tdown​=16 s.
  • Pre-copy. Vm​=1000 MB, R=100 MB/s, r=0.5, n=2, Tres​=0.5 s? Tdown​=0.25×10+0.5=3.0 s; Tmig​=10×1.75+0.5=18.0 s. Variant: Vm​=1024 MB, R=100 MB/s, r=0.2, n=3, Tres​=0.1 s? Tmig​≈12.88 s; Tdown​≈0.18 s.

Week 11 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 11 notes

  • Dew = independence + collaboration; Dropbox/Drive = storage-in-dew; App Store/Play = software-in-dew; GitHub = platform-in-dew; iCloud = IaD; DBiD = two DB copies (reliability).
  • Serverless: event-driven, granular, provider manages servers, pay per use; FaaS (your stateless functions; Lambda ~15 min) vs BaaS (Firebase-style back ends).

Likely question types: dew category ↔︎ example · FaaS vs BaaS · serverless drawback “which is NOT” · Lambda term ↔︎ meaning · sustainable-model component ↔︎ role.

Week 12 — must-remember

→ open the full Week 12 notes

  • 5G: ~10 Gbps, ~1 ms; eMBB (AR/VR) · URLLC (autonomous vehicles, telesurgery, smart grid) · mMTC (massive IoT). 5G–cloud: cloud must meet 5G (edge/MEC/fog); 5G cloudified via NFV/SDN.

Top traps

→ classification sheet · → high-yield list · → practice MCQs · → your practice sets

  1. NIST has 5 characteristics — virtualization/multi-tenancy are not among them.
  2. Azure = PaaS in the lecture; App Engine PaaS; Compute Engine IaaS.
  3. Public = low up-front cost; on-site private = limited resources; outsourced private = two perimeters.
  4. Para-virtualization modifies the guest; Popek–Goldberg needs sensitive ⊆ privileged.
  5. Valid ⇒ well-formed; XSD cannot declare entities.
  6. U compares with P/A (peak ÷ average), and Cv​ shrinks by 1/n​.
  7. GFS read = one replica; append = all, primary picks offset; quorum is strictly >.
  8. Mapper fails → redo all; reducer fails → only unfinished.
  9. Swift = object, Cinder = block.
  10. Use scheduled hours for availability; lower availability → bigger credit.
  11. Traffic analysis is passive; replay is active.
  12. Gartner = 7 risks; RPO = data, RTO = time.
  13. Offload only when compute-heavy & data-light.
  14. Fog: one hop, wireless, location-aware; cloud: multi-hop, leased line.
  15. Bursting/broker loose, aggregated partial, multi-tier tight.
  16. Live migration: total time ↑, downtime ↓; post-copy sends CPU first.
  17. Image ≠ container; rmi images vs rm containers; commit container → image.
  18. Two energy splits: DC (cooling 45 %) vs components (processor 45 %).
  19. FaaS ≠ BaaS; serverless still uses servers.
  20. In the health case the confirmatory module stays in the cloud.
  21. S3 = 99 % in the lecture’s SLA table (EC2 99.5 %, Microsoft 99.9 %). Your L11 set keys 99.9 %; choose 99 % whenever it is offered.
  22. SLA P1: the lecture’s 96.92 % and the standard 97.01 % can both appear as options. The key follows the lecture.
  23. Meghamala’s Dropbox-like service is Meghadata (not “Meghaduta”); its 3 OS images are Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora.
  24. Security goals = prevention, detection, recovery. “Retaliation” is a distractor.
